title: Definition of Terms in Research (With Examples) | AnswerThis
summary: Learn how to write the definition of terms in research: which terms to define, conceptual vs operational definitions, five steps and examples.
body_markdown:
The definition of terms in research is a short list of the key terms in your study and the meaning each one has in it. It tells readers exactly what you mean by each word, so no one reads your study in a different way.


In a Philippine thesis, this list usually appears in Chapter 1. This guide explains which terms to define, how conceptual and operational definitions differ, and how to write the section in five steps. It ends with examples from education, nursing, business and IT.


## The definition of terms: what it is and why it matters


The definition of terms is a section of your thesis that explains the important words in your study. Each entry names one term and gives its meaning.


Readers need it because many words have more than one meaning. “Performance” can mean a grade, a test score or a supervisor’s rating. Your definition tells the reader which one you mean.


A good entry does two jobs. It gives the general meaning of the term, usually from a published source. It also says how you will measure or observe that term in your own study.


## Where it goes in a Philippine thesis


In most Philippine theses, the definition of terms appears near the end of Chapter 1. It usually comes after the[significance of the study](https://answerthis.io/blog/significance-of-the-study) and the scope and delimitation. Generally, it is[placed](https://sites.google.com/deped.gov.ph/practicalresearch120232024/chapter-3/definition-of-terms) at the beginning of the research paper.


Schools differ. Some use a different heading, such as Operational Definition of Terms. Others place the section somewhere else. Follow your school’s thesis manual, and ask your adviser when the manual is silent.


## Which terms to define, and which to leave out


Define only the terms, words or phrases that have a special meaning in your study.


Define these terms:


-


The variables in your title and research questions. If you are not sure which ones they are, our guide to[independent and dependent variables](https://answerthis.io/blog/independent-and-dependent-variables) shows how to find them.


-


Words with a narrow or technical meaning in your study, such as “blended learning” or “medication adherence”.


-


Abbreviations you use often, such as GWA for general weighted average.


Leave these out:


-


Common words every reader knows, such as “students” or “teachers”, unless you use them in a special way.


-


Terms you mention once and never use again.


Use a quick test. If two readers could take a word in two different ways, define it.


## Conceptual vs operational definitions


Most schools ask for two kinds of definition for each term.


-


A conceptual definition gives the general meaning of the term. It works like a dictionary definition, but it comes from a book, journal article or other source in your field.


-


An operational definition says how you will measure or observe the term in your study. It names the instrument, the score or the record you will use.


[Conceptual definitions](https://uta.pressbooks.pub/advancedresearchmethodsinsw/chapter/10-3-operational-definitions/) are like dictionary definitions, because they explain a concept using other concepts. Whereas operationalisation is spelling out exactly how a concept will be measured.


The labels change from one source to another. The definition taken from published sources is termed “theoretical” and the researcher’s own definition “conceptual”. Many schools and guides use “conceptual” and “operational” instead. The idea is the same in both. Use the labels your school uses.


Here is one term defined both ways.


-


Conceptual:[P](https://doi.org/10.1037/0033-2909.133.1.65)[rocrastination](https://psycnet.apa.org/doiLanding?doi=10.1037%2F0033-2909.133.1.65) is defined as voluntarily delaying an intended course of action despite expecting to be worse off for the delay.


-


Operational: Academic procrastination refers to the respondent’s total score on a 10-item procrastination questionnaire answered on a 5-point scale. A higher score means more procrastination.


The table defines three more terms both ways. The conceptual meanings here are general descriptions for this example. In your own paper, take each one from a source and cite it.


Term


Conceptual definition (general meaning)


Operational definition (in this study)


Academic performance


How well a student meets the learning goals of a course or program


The respondent’s general weighted average (GWA) for the first semester, taken from registrar records


Screen time


The time a person spends using devices with a screen, such as phones, tablets and computers


The average hours per day of phone use shown in the phone’s screen time report over 7 days


Sleep quality


How well a person sleeps, including how long and how deeply they sleep


The respondent’s total score on the sleep questionnaire described in Chapter 3


The operational definition is the one your adviser will check most closely. It must match the way you collect data in Chapter 3. The diagram below follows one term from its general meaning to the data you will collect.

## How to write the definition of terms in 5 steps


### 1. List the terms


Go through your title, your statement of the problem and your hypotheses. Write down every variable and every word with a special meaning.


If your hypotheses are still a draft, the AnswerThis[hypothesis generator](https://answerthis.io/hypothesis-generator) can help. It drafts three pairs of null and alternative hypotheses, each with variables, a population and suggested measurements. Treat them as candidates to discuss with your adviser, not as findings.


### 2. Find a source for each conceptual meaning


Look for the meaning of each term in a textbook, journal article or professional dictionary in your field. A general dictionary is a weak source for technical terms. Save the source details as you go, so you can cite them later.


### 3. Say how you measure or observe each term


Write the operational definition. Name the instrument, the score, the record or the observation you will use. Start it with “In this study,” so readers can tell it apart from the conceptual meaning.


Your operational definitions must match your[Chapter 3 methodology](https://answerthis.io/blog/chapter-3-research) . Our guide to the[research instrument](https://answerthis.io/blog/research-instrument) explains how to choose and describe the tool you will use to collect data.


If your Chapter 3 plan is not ready, the AnswerThis[methodology generator](https://answerthis.io/methodology-generator) organizes a study plan into design, participants, procedure, measures and analysis. It keeps missing decisions as placeholders and gives 3 free runs. To validate a measure, check your instrument with your adviser.


### 4. Arrange the terms alphabetically


Use alphabetical order. It makes each term easy to find. If your school asks for a different order, follow it.


### 5. Cite your sources


Cite every conceptual definition you take from a source, in the citation style your school uses. Don't forget to acknowledge sources. Your operational definitions are your own, so they do not need a citation.


Each entry usually follows the same pattern. It starts with the term, gives the conceptual meaning with its citation, and ends with the operational definition. The sample page below shows this layout.


*A sample Definition of Terms page: entries in alphabetical order, each with a cited conceptual meaning and an operational definition that begins with “In this study”.*


To see how AnswerThis drafts the background, aims and methods of a study with citations, follow our tutorial on[drafting a research proposal](https://answerthis.io/guide/steps-to-draft-a-research-proposal-using-answerthis) . Your terms come from that same plan.


## Definition of terms examples from four fields


The examples below show how one term can be defined in each field. The conceptual meanings are short general descriptions. In your paper, take each one from a source and cite it.


### Education


Term


Conceptual meaning


Operational definition


Blended learning


Teaching that combines face-to-face classes with online learning


In this study, blended learning refers to Grade 11 classes that meet face-to-face twice a week and online three times a week.


Reading comprehension


The ability to understand and draw meaning from a written text


In this study, reading comprehension refers to the respondent’s score on the school’s 40-item reading test.


### Nursing


Term


Conceptual meaning


Operational definition


Medication adherence


The extent to which a patient takes medicine as prescribed


In this study, medication adherence refers to the percentage of prescribed doses the patient took in the past 30 days, based on pill counts during home visits.


Patient satisfaction


A patient’s judgment of the care they received


In this study, patient satisfaction refers to the respondent’s mean score on the hospital’s 15-item satisfaction survey.


### Business


Term


Conceptual meaning


Operational definition


Customer loyalty


A customer’s tendency to keep buying from the same business


In this study, customer loyalty refers to the number of purchases a customer made in the past six months, based on loyalty card records.


Work motivation


The drive that leads an employee to start and keep working toward goals


In this study, work motivation refers to the respondent’s mean score on the motivation questionnaire in Chapter 3.


### Information technology


Term


Conceptual meaning


Operational definition


System usability


How easily and effectively people can use a system


In this study, system usability refers to the respondent’s score on the System Usability Scale (SUS), a 10-item questionnaire scored from 0 to 100.


Response time


The time a system takes to react to a request


In this study, response time refers to the average time in seconds between a user’s request and the system’s reply, measured over 50 test runs.


## Common mistakes


-


Copying a general dictionary definition for a technical term. Use a source from your field instead.


-


Defining common words. A list full of everyday words hides the terms that matter.


-


Writing an operational definition that does not match your instrument. If Chapter 1 says “GWA” but Chapter 3 uses a test score, your adviser will ask you to fix one of them.


-


Defining a term one way and using it another way later in the paper.


-


Leaving out citations for definitions you took from a source.


## Conclusion


A clear definition of terms keeps your thesis consistent from Chapter 1 to Chapter 5. Choose only the terms that need it, give each a cited meaning, and make every operational definition match what you actually measure in Chapter 3. When those three things line up, your adviser and your panel read every result the way you meant it.


## FAQs


### What is the difference between a conceptual and an operational definition?


A conceptual definition gives the general meaning of a term, usually from a published source. An operational definition says how you will measure or observe that term in your study, such as a test score or a record.


### Where do I put the definition of terms in my thesis?


In most Philippine theses, it appears near the end of Chapter 1, after the scope and delimitation. Schools differ, so check your thesis manual.


### How many terms should I define?


There is no fixed number. Define every variable in your title and research questions, plus any word with a special meaning in your study. Keep the list short, so the important terms stand out.


### Do I need to cite the definition of terms?


Yes, for every conceptual definition you take from a book, article or dictionary. Your operational definitions are your own, so they need no citation.


### Should the definition of terms be arranged alphabetically?


Yes, most schools ask for alphabetical order. If your school’s manual asks for a different order, follow the manual.
